image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Standalone single-storey Flash Express parcel shop building, detailed front elevation with a glazed frontage and service counter at the window under a saturated yellow fascia carrying the black Flash Express wordmark and lightning device on a backlit sign, a yellow roller shutter box above the opening and parcel shelving visible inside, plain rendered side and rear walls with a wide roller loading shutter, flat roof with a low parapet and roof-mounted air-conditioning condensers Materials: yellow printed acrylic sign face and yellow painted panel at the front, plate glass, flat painted render on side and rear walls, galvanised shutter and roof plant.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow. Apart from the building's own signage described above, there is no other text or lettering anywhere in the frame.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Real trademark: Flash Express. The repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark; anyone shipping it needs their own trademark clearance.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.83 -- not a pass self-score. 848/16000 triangles, 11/12 draw calls, 8/8 materials, 11/16 unique geometries. Every critical feature is at or above its threshold; the one that was not was fixed rather than rescored.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope built at exactly 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 m against the declared 8 x 4.6 x 7.
featureReviews.notes: Three separate corrections got it there, all caught by check-coplanar or the envelope measurement rather than by eye: the parapet band's bottom sat at y=3.500 with the roof deck's bottom (51 m2 of coplanar co-facing surface) and its top at y=4.600 with the coping's top (53 m2 more); and the side coping runs, sized from a sibling with a different shell setback, overhung the rear by 0.03 m and pushed the prop to 7.03 m deep. Meshy reads this plate 29% taller than the declared module -- the building really is tall and narrow -- but the declaration is the kit's shared retail module and wins.

featureReviews.evidence: Yellow lightbox #E7DF4C (PBR confidence 0.829) in a dark border standing proud of the parapet, carrying black FLASH over EXPRESS with a drawn LIGHTNING BOLT in place of the S.
featureReviews.notes: This feature first scored 0.84 and the pass gate refused to advance -- correctly. The bolt is the single most recognisable thing about the mark, no font can set it, and a glyph substitute would read as a typo. Rather than argue the score up or relax the threshold, the canvas route gained a polygon primitive and the wordmark is now split either side of a drawn bolt. The score moved because the model changed.

featureReviews.evidence: Yellow jambs either side of the glazing and a lintel cantilevering over it, all one material and one draw call.
featureReviews.notes: The lintel is 0.40 m deep, reaching z=3.50 exactly -- the declared envelope face. At 0.42 it pushed the prop past its declared depth.

featureReviews.evidence: 22 ribbed slats filling most of the +X wall under a grey lintel, at #9AA1A7 (PBR confidence 0.831).
featureReviews.notes: The largest shutter in the retail set and the clearest feature on this building after the sign. Slats alternate by thinning INWARD, so no face reaches the parapet's 4.00 plane.

featureReviews.evidence: Pale coping (#9EA2A6, PBR confidence 0.726) capping front, sides and rear, inset from the parapet faces, sharing its component with the shutter lintel.
featureReviews.notes: Grouped by MATERIAL rather than location, which is what puts a roofline coping and a lintel on the +X wall in the same submission.

notes: Built on the shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m building module: detailed front elevation, plain rendered side and rear walls, no loose objects outside. Saturated yellow livery with the black wordmark and a WHITE lightning device with a black outline. Shopfront centred on the facade, with a hinged entrance door (door-hinge pivot) on the right and a yellow delivery counter with a small hatch opening in the glazing on the left. The rear roller loading shutter is part of the building, not a separate object.
